desc.4.1: Understanding the organization and its context — The organization shall determine external and internal issues that are relevant to its purpose and that affect its ability to achieve the intended outcome(s) of its information security management system.
desc.4.2: Understanding needs and expectations of interested parties — The organization shall determine interested parties that are relevant to the ISMS, the requirements of these interested parties, and which of these requirements will be addressed.
desc.4.3: Determining the scope of the information security management system — The organization shall determine the boundaries and applicability of the ISMS to establish its scope.
desc.4.4: Information security management system — The organization shall establish, implement, maintain and continually improve an information security management system, including the processes needed and their interactions.
desc.5.1: Leadership and commitment — Top management shall demonstrate leadership and commitment with respect to the ISMS by directing and supporting persons to contribute to the effectiveness of the ISMS and promoting continual improvement.
desc.5.2: Policy — Top management shall establish an information security policy that is appropriate to the purpose of the organization and provides a framework for setting information security objectives.
desc.5.3: Organizational roles, responsibilities and authorities — Top management shall ensure that the responsibilities and authorities for roles relevant to information security are assigned and communicated.
desc.6.1.1: General (Actions to address risks and opportunities) — When planning for the ISMS, the organization shall consider issues, requirements, and determine the risks and opportunities that need to be addressed.
desc.6.1.2: Information security risk assessment — The organization shall define and apply an information security risk assessment process that establishes and maintains information security risk criteria.
desc.6.1.3: Information security risk treatment — The organization shall define and apply an information security risk treatment process to select appropriate information security risk treatment options.
desc.6.1.3(d): Statement of Applicability (SoA) — The organization shall produce a Statement of Applicability (SoA) that contains the necessary controls and justification for inclusions or exclusions.
desc.6.2: Information security objectives and planning to achieve them — The organization shall establish information security objectives at relevant functions and levels. The objectives shall be measurable (if practicable).
desc.7.1: Resources — The organization shall determine and provide the resources needed for the establishment, implementation, maintenance and continual improvement of the ISMS.
desc.7.2: Competence — The organization shall determine the necessary competence of person(s) doing work under its control that affects its information security performance.
desc.7.3: Awareness — Persons doing work under the organization's control shall be aware of the information security policy and their contribution to the effectiveness of the ISMS.
desc.7.4: Communication — The organization shall determine the need for internal and external communications relevant to the information security management system.
desc.7.5: Documented information — The organization's ISMS shall include documented information required by this document and determined as necessary for the effectiveness of the ISMS.
desc.8.1: Operational planning and control — The organization shall plan, implement and control the processes needed to meet information security requirements, and to implement the actions determined in Clause 6.
desc.8.2: Information security risk assessment (Operational) — The organization shall perform information security risk assessments at planned intervals or when significant changes are proposed or occur.
desc.8.3: Information security risk treatment (Operational) — The organization shall implement the information security risk treatment plan. The organization shall retain documented information of the results.
desc.9.1: Monitoring, measurement, analysis and evaluation — The organization shall evaluate the information security performance and the effectiveness of the ISMS. It shall determine what needs to be monitored and measured.
desc.9.2: Internal audit — The organization shall conduct internal audits at planned intervals to provide information on whether the ISMS conforms to requirements and is effectively implemented.
desc.9.3: Management review — Top management shall review the organization's information security management system at planned intervals to ensure its continuing suitability, adequacy and effectiveness.
desc.10.1: Continual improvement — The organization shall continually improve the suitability, adequacy and effectiveness of the information security management system.
desc.10.2: Nonconformity and corrective action — When a nonconformity occurs, the organization shall react to the nonconformity, evaluate the need for action to eliminate causes, and implement corrective actions.
desc.A.5.1: Policies for information security — Information security policy and topic-specific policies should be defined, approved by management, published, communicated to and acknowledged by relevant personnel and relevant interested parties, and reviewed at planned intervals and if significant changes occur.
desc.A.5.2: Information security roles and responsibilities — Information security roles and responsibilities should be defined and allocated according to the organization needs.
desc.A.5.3: Segregation of duties — Conflicting duties and conflicting areas of responsibility should be segregated.
desc.A.5.4: Management responsibilities — Management should require all personnel to apply information security in accordance with the established information security policy, topic-specific policies and procedures of the organization.
desc.A.5.5: Contact with authorities — The organization should establish and maintain contact with relevant authorities.
desc.A.5.6: Contact with special interest groups — The organization should establish and maintain contact with special interest groups or other specialist security forums and professional associations.
desc.A.5.7: Threat intelligence — Information relating to information security threats should be collected and analysed to produce threat intelligence.
desc.A.5.8: Information security in project management — Information security should be integrated into project management.
desc.A.5.9: Inventory of information and other associated assets — An inventory of information and other associated assets, including owners, should be developed and maintained.
desc.A.5.10: Acceptable use of information and other associated assets — Rules for the acceptable use and procedures for handling information and other associated assets should be identified, documented and implemented.
desc.A.5.11: Return of assets — Personnel and other interested parties as appropriate should return all the organization's assets in their possession upon change or termination of their employment, contract or agreement.
desc.A.5.12: Classification of information — Information should be classified according to the information security needs of the organization based on confidentiality, integrity, availability and relevant interested party requirements.
desc.A.5.13: Labelling of information — An appropriate set of procedures for information labelling should be developed and implemented in accordance with the information classification scheme adopted by the organization.
desc.A.5.14: Information transfer — Information transfer rules, procedures, or agreements should be in place for all types of transfer facilities within the organization and between the organization and other parties.
desc.A.5.15: Access control — Rules to control physical and logical access to information and other associated assets should be established and implemented based on business and information security requirements.
desc.A.5.16: Identity management — The full life cycle of identities should be managed.
desc.A.5.17: Authentication information — Allocation and management of authentication information should be controlled by a management process, including advising personnel on the appropriate handling of authentication information.
desc.A.5.18: Access rights — Access rights to information and other associated assets should be provisioned, reviewed, modified and removed in accordance with the organization's topic-specific policy on and rules for access control.
desc.A.5.19: Information security in supplier relationships — Processes and procedures should be defined and implemented to manage the information security risks associated with the use of supplier's products or services.
desc.A.5.20: Addressing info security within supplier agreements — Relevant information security requirements should be established and agreed with each supplier based on the type of supplier relationship.
desc.A.5.21: Managing info security in the ICT supply chain — Processes and procedures should be defined and implemented to manage the information security risks associated with the ICT products and services supply chain.
desc.A.5.22: Monitoring, review & change mgmt of supplier services — The organization should regularly monitor, review, evaluate and manage change in supplier information security practices and service delivery.
desc.A.5.23: Information security for use of cloud services — Processes for acquisition, use, management and exit from cloud services should be established in accordance with the organization's information security requirements.
desc.A.5.24: Incident management planning and preparation — The organization should plan and prepare for managing information security incidents by defining, establishing and communicating information security incident management processes, roles and responsibilities.
desc.A.5.25: Assessment and decision on security events — The organization should assess information security events and decide if they are to be categorized as information security incidents.
desc.A.5.26: Response to information security incidents — Information security incidents should be responded to in accordance with the documented procedures.
desc.A.5.27: Learning from information security incidents — Knowledge gained from information security incidents should be used to strengthen and improve the information security controls.
desc.A.5.28: Collection of evidence — The organization should establish and implement procedures for the identification, collection, acquisition and preservation of evidence related to information security events.
desc.A.5.29: Information security during disruption — The organization should plan how to maintain information security at an appropriate level during disruption.
desc.A.5.30: ICT readiness for business continuity — ICT readiness should be planned, implemented, maintained and tested based on business continuity objectives and ICT continuity requirements.
desc.A.5.31: Legal, statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements — Legal, statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements relevant to information security and the organization's approach to meet these requirements should be identified, documented and kept up to date.
desc.A.5.32: Intellectual property rights — The organization should implement appropriate procedures to protect intellectual property rights.
desc.A.5.33: Protection of records — Records should be protected from loss, destruction, falsification, unauthorized access and unauthorized release.
desc.A.5.34: Privacy and protection of PII — The organization should identify and meet the requirements regarding the preservation of privacy and protection of PII according to applicable laws and regulations and contractual requirements.
desc.A.5.35: Independent review of information security — The organization's approach to managing information security and its implementation including people, processes and technologies should be reviewed independently at planned intervals, or when significant changes occur.
desc.A.5.36: Compliance with policies, rules and standards — Compliance with the organization's information security policy, topic-specific policies, rules and standards should be regularly reviewed.
desc.A.5.37: Documented operating procedures — Operating procedures for information processing facilities should be documented and made available to personnel who need them.
desc.A.6.1: Screening — Background verification checks on all candidates to become personnel should be carried out prior to joining the organization and on an ongoing basis taking into consideration applicable laws, regulations and ethics and proportional to the business requirements, the classification of the information to be accessed and the perceived risks.
desc.A.6.2: Terms and conditions of employment — The employment contractual agreements should state the personnel's and the organization's responsibilities for information security.
desc.A.6.3: Information security awareness, education and training — Personnel of the organization and relevant interested parties should receive appropriate information security awareness, education and training and regular updates of the organization's information security policy, topic-specific policies and procedures, as relevant for their job function.
desc.A.6.4: Disciplinary process — A disciplinary process should be formalized and communicated to take action against personnel and other relevant interested parties who have committed an information security policy violation.
desc.A.6.5: Responsibilities after termination or change — Information security responsibilities and duties that remain valid after termination or change of employment should be defined, enforced and communicated to relevant personnel and other interested parties.
desc.A.6.6: Confidentiality or non-disclosure agreements — Confidentiality or non-disclosure agreements reflecting the organization's needs for the protection of information should be identified, documented, regularly reviewed and signed by personnel and other relevant interested parties.
desc.A.6.7: Remote working — Security measures should be implemented when personnel are working remotely to protect information accessed, processed or stored outside the organization's premises.
desc.A.6.8: Information security event reporting — The organization should provide a mechanism for personnel to report observed or suspected information security events through appropriate channels in a timely manner.
desc.A.7.1: Physical security perimeters — Security perimeters should be defined and used to protect areas that contain information and other associated assets.
desc.A.7.2: Physical entry — Secure areas should be protected by appropriate entry controls and access points.
desc.A.7.3: Securing offices, rooms and facilities — Physical security for offices, rooms and facilities should be designed and implemented.
desc.A.7.4: Physical security monitoring — Premises should be continuously monitored for unauthorized physical access.
desc.A.7.5: Protecting against physical and environmental threats — Protection against physical and environmental threats, such as natural disasters and other intentional or unintentional physical threats to infrastructure should be designed and implemented.
desc.A.7.6: Working in secure areas — Security measures for working in secure areas should be designed and implemented.
desc.A.7.7: Clear desk and clear screen — Clear desk rules for papers and removable storage media and clear screen rules for information processing facilities should be defined and appropriately enforced.
desc.A.7.8: Equipment siting and protection — Equipment should be sited securely and protected.
desc.A.7.9: Security of assets off-premises — Information and other associated assets off-premises should be protected.
desc.A.7.10: Storage media — Storage media should be managed through their life cycle of acquisition, use, transportation and disposal in accordance with the organization's classification scheme and handling requirements.
desc.A.7.11: Supporting utilities — Information processing facilities should be protected from power failures and other disruptions caused by failures in supporting utilities.
desc.A.7.12: Cabling security — Cables carrying power, data or supporting information services should be protected from interception, interference or damage.
desc.A.7.13: Equipment maintenance — Equipment should be maintained correctly to ensure availability, integrity and confidentiality of information.
desc.A.7.14: Secure disposal or re-use of equipment — Items of equipment containing storage media should be verified to ensure that any sensitive data and licensed software has been removed or securely overwritten prior to disposal or re-use.
desc.A.8.1: User endpoint devices — Information stored on, processed by or routed via user endpoint devices should be protected.
desc.A.8.2: Privileged access rights — The allocation and use of privileged access rights should be restricted and managed.
desc.A.8.3: Information access restriction — Access to information and other associated assets should be restricted in accordance with the established topic-specific policy on access control.
desc.A.8.4: Access to source code — Read and write access to source code, development tools and software libraries should be appropriately managed.
desc.A.8.5: Secure authentication — Secure authentication technologies and procedures should be implemented based on information access restrictions and the topic-specific policy on access control.
desc.A.8.6: Capacity management — The use of resources should be monitored and adjusted in line with current and projected capacity requirements.
desc.A.8.7: Protection against malware — Protection against malware should be implemented and supported by appropriate user awareness.
desc.A.8.8: Management of technical vulnerabilities — Information about technical vulnerabilities of information systems in use should be obtained, the organization's exposure to such vulnerabilities should be evaluated and appropriate measures should be taken.
desc.A.8.9: Configuration management — Configurations, including security configurations, of hardware, software, services and networks should be established, documented, implemented, monitored and reviewed.
desc.A.8.10: Information deletion — Information stored in information systems, devices or in any other storage media should be deleted when no longer required.
desc.A.8.11: Data masking — Data masking should be used in accordance with the organization's topic-specific policy on access control and other related topic-specific policies, and business requirements, taking into consideration applicable legislation.
desc.A.8.12: Data leakage prevention — Data leakage prevention measures should be applied to systems, networks and any other devices that process, store or transmit sensitive information.
desc.A.8.13: Information backup — Backup copies of information, software and systems should be maintained and regularly tested in accordance with the agreed topic-specific policy on backup.
desc.A.8.14: Redundancy of information processing facilities — Information processing facilities should be implemented with redundancy sufficient to meet availability requirements.
desc.A.8.15: Logging — Logs that record activities, exceptions, faults and other relevant events should be produced, stored, protected and analysed.
desc.A.8.16: Monitoring activities — Networks, systems and applications should be monitored for anomalous behaviour and appropriate actions taken to evaluate potential information security incidents.
desc.A.8.17: Clock synchronisation — The clocks of information processing systems used by the organization should be synchronized to approved time sources.
desc.A.8.18: Use of privileged utility programs — The use of utility programs that can be capable of overriding system and application controls should be restricted and tightly controlled.
desc.A.8.19: Installation of software on operational systems — Procedures and measures should be implemented to securely manage software installation on operational systems.
desc.A.8.20: Networks security — Networks and network devices should be secured, managed and controlled to protect information in systems and applications.
desc.A.8.21: Security of network services — Security mechanisms, service levels and management requirements of network services should be identified, implemented and monitored.
desc.A.8.22: Segregation of networks — Groups of information services, users and information systems should be segregated in the organization's networks.
desc.A.8.23: Web filtering — Access to external websites should be managed to reduce exposure to malicious content.
desc.A.8.24: Use of cryptography — Rules for the effective and acceptable use of cryptography, including cryptographic key management, should be defined and implemented.
desc.A.8.25: Secure development life cycle — Rules for the secure development of software and systems should be established and applied.
desc.A.8.26: Application security requirements — Information security requirements should be identified, specified and approved when developing or acquiring applications.
desc.A.8.27: Secure system architecture and engineering principles — Principles for engineering secure systems should be established, documented, maintained and applied to any information system development activities.
desc.A.8.28: Secure coding — Secure coding principles should be applied to software development.
desc.A.8.29: Security testing in development and acceptance — Security testing processes should be defined and implemented in the development life cycle.
desc.A.8.30: Outsourced development — The organization should direct, monitor and review the activities related to outsourced system development.
desc.A.8.31: Separation of dev, test and production environments — Development, testing and production environments should be separated and secured.
desc.A.8.32: Change management — Changes to information processing facilities and information systems should be subject to change management procedures.
desc.A.8.33: Test information — Test information should be appropriately selected, protected and managed.
desc.A.8.34: Protection of info systems during audit testing — Audit tests and other assurance activities involving assessment of operational systems should be planned and agreed between the tester and appropriate management.

desc.GV: GOVERN — The organisation's cybersecurity risk management strategy, expectations, and policy are established, communicated, and monitored. GOVERN is new in CSF 2.0 and provides the overarching context for all other functions.
desc.GV.OC: Organizational Context — The circumstances surrounding the organisation's cybersecurity risk management decisions are understood
desc.GV.OC-01: Organizational mission is understood and informs cybersecurity risk management — The organisational mission is understood and informs cybersecurity risk management.
desc.GV.OC-02: Internal and external stakeholders are understood, and their needs and expectations regarding cybersecurity risk management are understood — Internal and external stakeholders are determined, and their needs and expectations regarding cybersecurity risk management are understood.
desc.GV.OC-03: Legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements regarding cybersecurity are understood and managed — Legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements regarding cybersecurity — including privacy and civil liberties obligations — are understood and managed.
desc.GV.OC-04: Critical objectives, capabilities, and services that external stakeholders depend on or expect from the organization are understood and communicated — Critical objectives, capabilities, and services that external stakeholders depend on or expect from the organisation are understood and communicated.
desc.GV.OC-05: Outcomes, capabilities, and services that the organization depends on are understood and communicated — Outcomes, capabilities, and services that the organisation depends on are understood and communicated.
desc.GV.OC-06: Conformance requirements are understood and met — Conformance requirements — whether from law, regulation, contract, or internal policy — are understood and met.
desc.GV.RM: Risk Management Strategy — The organisation's priorities, constraints, risk tolerance, and assumptions are established and used to support operational risk decisions
desc.GV.RM-01: Risk management objectives are established and agreed to by organizational stakeholders — Risk management objectives are established and agreed to by organisational stakeholders.
desc.GV.RM-02: Risk appetite and risk tolerance statements are established, communicated, and maintained — Risk appetite and risk tolerance statements are established, communicated, and maintained.
desc.GV.RM-03: Cybersecurity risk management activities and outcomes are included in enterprise risk management processes — Cybersecurity risk management activities and outcomes are included in enterprise risk management processes.
desc.GV.RM-04: Strategic direction that describes appropriate risk response options is established and communicated — Strategic direction that describes appropriate risk response options is established and communicated.
desc.GV.RM-05: Lines of communication across the organization are established for cybersecurity risks, including risks from suppliers and other third parties — Lines of communication across the organisation are established for cybersecurity risks, including risks from suppliers and other third parties.
desc.GV.RM-06: A standardized method for calculating, documenting, categorizing, and prioritizing cybersecurity risks is established and communicated — A standardised method for calculating, documenting, categorising, and prioritising cybersecurity risks is established and communicated.
desc.GV.RM-07: Strategic opportunities (i.e., positive risks) are characterized and are included in organizational cybersecurity risk discussions — Strategic opportunities (positive risks) are characterised and included in organisational cybersecurity risk discussions.
desc.GV.RR: Roles, Responsibilities, and Authorities — Cybersecurity roles, responsibilities, and authorities to foster accountability, performance assessment, and continuous improvement are established and communicated
desc.GV.RR-01: Organizational leadership is responsible and accountable for cybersecurity risk and fosters a culture that is risk-aware, ethical, and continually improving — Organisational leadership is responsible and accountable for cybersecurity risk and fosters a culture of cybersecurity risk awareness.
desc.GV.RR-02: Roles, responsibilities, and authorities related to cybersecurity risk management are established, communicated, and enforced — Roles, responsibilities, and authorities related to cybersecurity risk management are established, communicated, and enforced.
desc.GV.RR-03: Adequate resources are allocated commensurate with the cybersecurity risk strategy, roles, responsibilities, and policies — Adequate resources are allocated commensurate with the cybersecurity risk strategy, roles, responsibilities, and policies.
desc.GV.RR-04: Cybersecurity is included in human resources practices — Cybersecurity is included in human resources practices (e.g., de-provisioning, personnel actions).
desc.GV.PO: Policy — Organisational cybersecurity policy is established, communicated, and enforced
desc.GV.PO-01: Policy for managing cybersecurity risks is established based on organizational context, cybersecurity strategy, and priorities and is communicated and enforced — A policy for managing cybersecurity risks is established based on organisational context, cybersecurity strategy, and priorities.
desc.GV.PO-02: Policy is reviewed, updated, communicated, and enforced to reflect changes in requirements, threats, technology, and organizational mission — Policy is reviewed, updated, communicated, and enforced to reflect changes in requirements, threats, technology, and organisational mission.
desc.GV.OV: Oversight — Results of organisation-wide cybersecurity risk management activities and performance are used to inform, improve, and adjust the risk management strategy
desc.GV.OV-01: Cybersecurity risk management strategy outcomes are reviewed to inform and adjust strategy and direction — Cybersecurity risk management strategy outcomes are reviewed to inform and adjust strategy and direction.
desc.GV.OV-02: The cybersecurity risk management strategy is reviewed and adjusted to ensure coverage of organizational requirements and risks — The cybersecurity risk management strategy is reviewed and adjusted to ensure coverage of organisational requirements and risks.
desc.GV.OV-03: Organizational cybersecurity risk management performance is evaluated and reviewed for adjustments needed — Organisational cybersecurity risk management performance is evaluated and reviewed for adjustments needed.
desc.GV.SC: Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management — Cyber supply chain risk management processes are identified, established, managed, monitored, and improved by organisational stakeholders
desc.GV.SC-01: A cybersecurity supply chain risk management program, strategy, objectives, policies, and processes are established and agreed to by organizational stakeholders — A cybersecurity supply chain risk management programme, strategy, objectives, policies, and processes are established and agreed to by organisational stakeholders.
desc.GV.SC-02: Cybersecurity roles and responsibilities for suppliers, customers, and partners are established, communicated, and coordinated internally and externally — Cybersecurity roles and responsibilities for suppliers, customers, and partners are established, communicated, and coordinated internally and externally.
desc.GV.SC-03: Cybersecurity supply chain risk management is integrated into cybersecurity and enterprise risk management, risk assessment, and improvement processes — Cybersecurity supply chain risk management is integrated into cybersecurity and enterprise risk management, risk assessment, and improvement processes.
desc.GV.SC-04: Suppliers are known and prioritized by criticality — Suppliers are known and prioritised by criticality.
desc.GV.SC-05: Requirements to address cybersecurity risks in supply chains are established, prioritized, and integrated into contracts and other agreements with suppliers and other relevant third parties — Requirements to address cybersecurity risks in supply chains are established, prioritised, and integrated into contracts and other agreements with suppliers and other relevant third parties.
desc.GV.SC-06: Planning and due diligence are performed to reduce risks before entering into formal supplier or other third-party relationships — Planning and due diligence are conducted to reduce risks before entering into formal supplier or other third-party relationships.
desc.GV.SC-07: The risks posed by a supplier, their products and services, and other third parties are understood, recorded, prioritized, assessed, responded to, and monitored over the course of the relationship — The risks posed by a supplier, their products and services, and other third parties are identified, recorded, prioritised, assessed, responded to, and monitored over the course of the relationship.
desc.GV.SC-08: Relevant suppliers and other third parties are included in incident planning, response, and recovery activities — Relevant suppliers and other third parties are included in incident planning, response, and recovery activities.
desc.GV.SC-09: Supply chain security practices are integrated into cybersecurity and enterprise risk management programs, and their performance is monitored throughout the technology product and service life cycle — Supply chain security practices are integrated into cybersecurity and enterprise risk management programmes, and their performance is monitored throughout the technology product and service life cycle.
desc.GV.SC-10: Cybersecurity supply chain risk management plans include provisions for activities that occur after the conclusion of a partnership or service agreement — Cybersecurity supply chain risk management plans include provisions for activities that occur after the conclusion of a partnership or service agreement.
desc.ID: IDENTIFY — The organisation's current cybersecurity risks are understood. This function supports identifying and prioritising the assets, vulnerabilities, threats, and risks most important to the organisation.
desc.ID.AM: Asset Management — Assets (data, hardware, software, systems, facilities, services, people) that enable the organisation to achieve business purposes are identified and managed consistent with their relative importance to organisational objectives and the organisation's risk strategy
desc.ID.AM-01: Inventories of hardware managed by the organization are maintained — Inventories of hardware managed by the organisation are maintained.
desc.ID.AM-02: Inventories of software, services, and systems managed by the organization are maintained — Inventories of software, services, and systems managed by the organisation are maintained.
desc.ID.AM-03: Representations of the organization's authorized network communication and internal and external network data flows are maintained — Representations of the organisation's authorised network communication and internal and external network data flows are maintained.
desc.ID.AM-04: Inventories of services provided by suppliers are maintained — Inventories of services provided by suppliers are maintained.
desc.ID.AM-05: Assets are prioritized based on classification, criticality, resources, and impact on the mission — Assets are prioritised based on classification, criticality, resources, and impact on the mission.
desc.ID.AM-06: Personnel are inventoried — Inventories of the organisation's personnel are maintained.
desc.ID.AM-07: Inventories of data and corresponding metadata for designated data types are maintained — Inventories of data and corresponding metadata for designated data types are maintained.
desc.ID.AM-08: Systems, hardware, software, services, and data are managed throughout their life cycles — Systems, hardware, software, services, and data are managed throughout their life cycles.
desc.ID.RA: Risk Assessment — The cybersecurity risk to the organisation, assets, and individuals is understood by the organisation
desc.ID.RA-01: Vulnerabilities in assets are identified, validated, and recorded — Vulnerabilities in assets are identified, validated, and recorded.
desc.ID.RA-02: Cyber threat intelligence is received from information sharing forums and sources — Cyber threat intelligence is received from information sharing forums and sources.
desc.ID.RA-03: Internal and external threats to the organization are identified and recorded — Internal and external threats to the organisation are identified and recorded.
desc.ID.RA-04: Potential impacts and likelihoods of threats exploiting vulnerabilities are identified and recorded — Potential impacts and likelihoods of threats exploiting vulnerabilities are identified and recorded.
desc.ID.RA-05: Threats, vulnerabilities, likelihoods, and impacts are used to understand inherent risk and inform risk response prioritization — Threats, vulnerabilities, likelihoods, and impacts are used to understand inherent risk and inform risk response prioritisation.
desc.ID.RA-06: Risk responses are chosen, prioritized, planned, tracked, and communicated — Risk responses are chosen, prioritised, planned, tracked, and communicated.
desc.ID.RA-07: Changes and exceptions are managed, assessed for risk impact, and recorded — Changes and exceptions are managed, assessed for risk impact, and recorded.
desc.ID.IM: Improvement — Improvements to organisational cybersecurity risk management processes, procedures and activities are identified across all CSF Functions
desc.ID.IM-01: Improvements are identified from evaluations — Improvements are identified from evaluations.
desc.ID.IM-02: Improvements are identified from security tests and exercises, including those done in coordination with suppliers and relevant third parties — Improvements are identified from security tests and exercises, including those done in coordination with suppliers and relevant third parties.
desc.ID.IM-03: Improvements are identified from execution of operational processes, procedures, and activities — Improvements are identified from execution of operational processes, procedures, and activities.
desc.ID.IM-04: Incident response plans and other cybersecurity plans that affect operations are established, communicated, maintained, and improved — Incident response plans and other cybersecurity plans that affect operations are established, communicated, maintained, and improved.
desc.PR: PROTECT — Safeguards to manage the organisation's cybersecurity risks are used. The PROTECT function supports the ability to prevent or reduce the likelihood and impact of cybersecurity events.
desc.PR.AA: Identity Management, Authentication, and Access Control — Access to physical and logical assets is limited to authorised users, services, and hardware, and is managed commensurate with the assessed risk of unauthorised access
desc.PR.AA-01: Identities and credentials for authorized users, services, and hardware are managed by the organization — Identities and credentials for authorised users, services, and hardware are managed by the organisation.
desc.PR.AA-02: Identities are proofed and bound to credentials based on the context of interactions — Identities are proofed and bound to credentials based on the context of interactions.
desc.PR.AA-03: Users, services, and hardware are authenticated — Users, services, and hardware are authenticated.
desc.PR.AA-04: Identity assertions are protected, conveyed, and verified — Identity assertions are protected, conveyed, and verified.
desc.PR.AA-05: Access permissions, entitlements, and authorizations are defined in a policy, managed, enforced, and reviewed, and incorporate the principles of least privilege and separation of duties — Access permissions, entitlements, and authorisations are defined in a policy, managed, enforced, and reviewed, and incorporate the principles of least privilege and separation of duties.
desc.PR.AA-06: Physical access to assets is managed, monitored, and enforced commensurate with risk — Physical access to assets is managed, monitored, and enforced commensurate with risk.
desc.PR.AT: Awareness and Training — The organisation's personnel are provided with cybersecurity awareness and training so that they can perform their cybersecurity-related tasks
desc.PR.AT-01: Personnel are provided with awareness and training so that they possess the knowledge and skills to perform general tasks with cybersecurity risks in mind — Personnel are provided cybersecurity awareness and training so that they can perform their cybersecurity-related tasks.
desc.PR.AT-02: Individuals in specialized roles are provided with awareness and training so that they possess the knowledge and skills to perform relevant tasks with cybersecurity risks in mind — Individuals in specialised roles are provided with cybersecurity awareness and training so that they possess the knowledge and skills to perform relevant tasks.
desc.PR.DS: Data Security — Data are managed consistent with the organisation's risk strategy to protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information
desc.PR.DS-01: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data at rest are protected — The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-at-rest are protected.
desc.PR.DS-02: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data in transit are protected — The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-in-transit are protected.
desc.PR.DS-10: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data in use are protected — The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data in use are protected.
desc.PR.DS-11: Backups of data are created, protected, maintained, and tested — Backups of data are created, protected, maintained, and tested.
desc.PR.PS: Platform Security — The hardware, software (e.g., firmware, operating systems, applications), and services of physical and virtual platforms are managed consistent with the organisation's risk strategy to protect their confidentiality, integrity, and availability
desc.PR.PS-01: Configuration management practices are established and applied — Configuration management practices are established and applied.
desc.PR.PS-02: Software is maintained, replaced, and removed commensurate with risk — Software is maintained, replaced, and removed commensurate with risk.
desc.PR.PS-03: Hardware is maintained, replaced, and removed commensurate with risk — Hardware is maintained, replaced, and removed commensurate with risk.
desc.PR.PS-04: Log records are generated and made available for continuous monitoring — Log records are generated and made available for continuous monitoring.
desc.PR.PS-05: Installation and execution of unauthorized software are prevented — Installation and execution of unauthorised software are prevented.
desc.PR.PS-06: Secure software development practices are integrated, and their performance is monitored throughout the software development life cycle — Secure software development practices are integrated, and their performance is monitored throughout the software development life cycle.

about.title: About NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0
about.blurb: The NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0 provides guidance to industry, government agencies, and other organisations to manage cybersecurity risks. It offers a taxonomy of high-level cybersecurity outcomes that can be used by any organisation — regardless of its size, sector, or maturity — to better understand, assess, prioritise, and communicate its cybersecurity efforts.

p: The NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0, published in February 2024, is a voluntary framework that provides organisations with a common language and systematic methodology for managing cybersecurity risk. It was developed through a collaborative process involving industry, government, and academia.

CSF 2.0 introduces a new sixth function — GOVERN — which sits at the centre of the framework and underscores that cybersecurity risk management must be embedded in organisational strategy, not treated as a purely technical concern.

The framework is designed to complement, not replace, existing cybersecurity programmes and risk management processes. It can be applied alongside other standards such as ISO/IEC 27001, NIST SP 800-53, and CIS Controls.

l: GOVERN (GV) — Establishes the organisational context, strategy, roles, and oversight needed to manage cybersecurity risk. New in CSF 2.0.
IDENTIFY (ID) — Helps the organisation understand its assets, risks, and improvement priorities.
PROTECT (PR) — Supports the ability to safeguard assets and limit the impact of cybersecurity events.
DETECT (DE) — Enables timely discovery of cybersecurity events and anomalies.
RESPOND (RS) — Supports the ability to contain and manage the impacts of a detected cybersecurity incident.
RECOVER (RC) — Supports timely restoration of normal operations and capabilities impaired by a cybersecurity incident.

p: The CSF Core is organised as a hierarchy: Functions → Categories → Subcategories. There are 6 Functions, 22 Categories, and 106 Subcategories. Each Subcategory represents a specific cybersecurity outcome — a concise statement of what 'good' looks like.

Organisations use the framework by creating Profiles — mappings of the CSF outcomes to their business requirements, risk tolerance, and resources. A 'Current Profile' captures the present state; a 'Target Profile' captures desired outcomes. The gap between them guides prioritisation.

CSF 2.0 and ISO/IEC 27001:2022 are complementary. ISO 27001 specifies requirements for an Information Security Management System (ISMS) and is certifiable; CSF 2.0 provides outcome-focused guidance and a risk communication vocabulary.

Mapping between the two frameworks allows organisations to demonstrate alignment with both without duplicating effort. Many ISO 27001 Annex A controls map directly to CSF 2.0 subcategories, enabling joint gap analyses and integrated audit programmes.

sections.name: Organizational Context
sections.desc: The circumstances surrounding the organisation's cybersecurity risk management decisions are understood

items.name: Organizational mission is understood and informs cybersecurity risk management
items.desc: The organisational mission is understood and informs cybersecurity risk management.
achieved: The organisational mission, vision, and strategic objectives are documented and reviewed regularly.
Cybersecurity risk tolerance is explicitly tied to and informed by the organisational mission.
Senior leadership has approved and communicates the connection between mission and cybersecurity priorities.
Business impact analyses reference the mission when classifying critical services and assets.
evidence: Organisational mission statement linked to cybersecurity risk appetite documentation
Board-approved cybersecurity strategy aligned to mission objectives
Risk tolerance statement referencing mission-critical functions
Business impact analysis referencing mission-critical processes

Evidence of monitoring regulatory change (e.g., legal update subscriptions, regulator communications)
Data protection impact assessments (DPIAs) or privacy risk assessments

desc.CC: Common Criteria (Security) — The Common Criteria are required for all SOC 2 engagements and form the security foundation. They map directly to the COSO Internal Control — Integrated Framework and cover nine areas from governance through to risk mitigation.
desc.CC1: Control Environment — The Control Environment criteria assess whether the organisation demonstrates commitment to integrity and ethical values, maintains appropriate oversight structures, attracts and retains competent personnel, and enforces accountability for internal control responsibilities.
desc.CC1.1: COSO Principle 1: Demonstrates commitment to integrity and ethical values — The entity demonstrates a commitment to integrity and ethical values.
desc.CC1.2: COSO Principle 2: Board exercises oversight responsibility — The board of directors demonstrates independence from management and exercises oversight of the development and performance of internal control.
desc.CC1.3: COSO Principle 3: Management establishes structures, reporting lines, and authorities — Management establishes, with board oversight, structures, reporting lines, and appropriate authorities and responsibilities in the pursuit of objectives.
desc.CC1.4: COSO Principle 4: Demonstrates commitment to attract, develop, and retain competent individuals — The entity demonstrates a commitment to attract, develop, and retain competent individuals in alignment with objectives.
desc.CC1.5: COSO Principle 5: Holds individuals accountable for internal control responsibilities — The entity holds individuals accountable for their internal control responsibilities in the pursuit of objectives.
desc.CC2: Communication and Information — The Communication and Information criteria assess whether the organisation generates, uses, and communicates relevant quality information both internally and externally to support the functioning of internal control.
desc.CC2.1: COSO Principle 13: Uses relevant information to support internal control — The entity obtains or generates and uses relevant, quality information to support the functioning of internal control.
desc.CC2.2: COSO Principle 14: Communicates internally to support internal control — The entity internally communicates information, including objectives and responsibilities for internal control, necessary to support the functioning of internal control.
desc.CC2.3: COSO Principle 15: Communicates externally — The entity communicates with external parties regarding matters affecting the functioning of internal control.
desc.CC3: Risk Assessment — The Risk Assessment criteria assess whether the organisation specifies suitable objectives, identifies and analyses risks to achieving those objectives, assesses fraud risk, and identifies and assesses changes that could affect the system of internal control.
desc.CC3.1: COSO Principle 6: Specifies suitable objectives — The entity specifies objectives with sufficient clarity to enable the identification and assessment of risks relating to objectives.
desc.CC3.2: COSO Principle 7: Identifies and analyses risk — The entity identifies risks to the achievement of its objectives across the entity and analyses risks as a basis for determining how the risks should be managed.
desc.CC3.3: COSO Principle 8: Assesses fraud risk — The entity considers the potential for fraud in assessing risks to the achievement of objectives.
desc.CC3.4: COSO Principle 9: Identifies and analyses significant change — The entity identifies and assesses changes that could significantly impact the system of internal control.
desc.CC4: Monitoring Activities — The Monitoring Activities criteria assess whether the organisation selects and performs ongoing evaluations to verify that components of internal control are present and functioning, and communicates deficiencies in a timely manner.
desc.CC4.1: COSO Principle 16: Conducts ongoing and/or separate evaluations — The entity selects, develops, and performs ongoing and/or separate evaluations to ascertain whether the components of internal control are present and functioning.
desc.CC4.2: COSO Principle 17: Evaluates and communicates deficiencies — The entity evaluates and communicates internal control deficiencies in a timely manner to those parties responsible for taking corrective action, including senior management and the board of directors as appropriate.
desc.CC5: Control Activities — The Control Activities criteria assess whether the organisation selects and develops general and technology-specific control activities, and deploys policies and procedures to support the achievement of objectives.
desc.CC5.1: COSO Principle 10: Selects and develops control activities — The entity selects and develops control activities that contribute to the mitigation of risks to the achievement of objectives to acceptable levels.
desc.CC5.2: COSO Principle 11: Selects and develops technology control activities — The entity also selects and develops general control activities over technology to support the achievement of objectives.
desc.CC5.3: COSO Principle 12: Deploys through policies and procedures — The entity deploys control activities through policies that establish what is expected and procedures that put policies into action.
desc.CC6: Logical and Physical Access Controls — The Logical and Physical Access Controls criteria address the most operationally detailed security requirements in the Common Criteria, covering identity management, access provisioning and de-provisioning, physical security, data transmission controls, and malware prevention.
desc.CC6.1: Implements logical access security software, infrastructure, and architectures — The entity implements logical access security software, infrastructure, and architectures over protected information assets to protect them from security events to meet the entity's objectives.
desc.CC6.2: Registers and authorises users prior to issuing credentials — Prior to issuing system credentials and granting system access, the entity registers and authorises new internal and external users whose access is administered by the entity.
desc.CC6.3: Authorises, modifies, or removes access based on roles — The entity authorises, modifies, or removes access to data, software, functions, and other protected information assets based on roles, responsibilities, or the system design and changes, in a timely manner.
desc.CC6.4: Restricts physical access to authorised personnel — The entity restricts physical access to facilities and protected information assets (for example, servers, backup media, printers) to authorised personnel to meet the entity's objectives.
desc.CC6.5: Discontinues protections over physical assets only after data has been made unreadable — The entity discontinues logical and physical protections over physical assets only after the ability to read or recover data and software from those assets has been diminished and is consistent with the entity's objectives.
desc.CC6.6: Implements logical access security measures against external threats — The entity implements logical access security measures to protect against threats from sources outside its system boundaries.
desc.CC6.7: Restricts transmission, movement, and removal of information — The entity restricts the transmission, movement, and removal of information to authorised internal and external users and processes, and protects it during transmission, movement, and removal to meet the entity's objectives.
desc.CC6.8: Prevents or detects introduction of unauthorised or malicious software — The entity implements controls to prevent or detect and act upon the introduction of unauthorised or malicious software to meet the entity's objectives.
desc.CC7: System Operations — The System Operations criteria address how the organisation detects and responds to security events, anomalies, and incidents, including recovery from identified security incidents.
desc.CC7.1: Detects and monitors for new vulnerabilities — To meet its objectives, the entity uses detection and monitoring procedures to identify (1) changes to configurations that result in the introduction of new vulnerabilities, and (2) susceptibilities to newly discovered vulnerabilities.
desc.CC7.2: Monitors system components for anomalies — The entity monitors system components and the operation of those components for anomalies that are indicative of malicious acts, natural disasters, and errors affecting the entity's ability to meet its objectives.
desc.CC7.3: Evaluates potential security events — The entity evaluates security events to determine whether they could or have resulted in a failure of the entity to meet its objectives (security incidents) and, if so, takes actions to prevent or address such failures.
desc.CC7.4: Responds to identified security incidents — The entity responds to identified security incidents by executing a defined incident response program to understand, contain, remediate, and communicate security incidents, as appropriate.
desc.CC7.5: Identifies and implements activities to recover from security incidents — The entity identifies, develops, and implements activities to recover from identified security incidents.
desc.CC8: Change Management — The Change Management criteria address whether changes to infrastructure, data, software, and procedures are authorised, designed, tested, approved, and implemented in a controlled manner.
desc.CC8.1: Authorises, designs, develops, tests, approves, and implements changes — The entity authorises, designs, develops or acquires, configures, documents, tests, approves, and implements changes to infrastructure, data, software, and procedures to meet its objectives.
desc.CC9: Risk Mitigation — The Risk Mitigation criteria address whether the organisation identifies and manages risks arising from business disruption, vendor relationships, and business partner dependencies.
desc.CC9.1: Identifies and mitigates risks from business disruption — The entity identifies, selects, and develops risk mitigation activities for risks arising from potential business disruptions.
desc.CC9.2: Assesses and manages risks from vendors and business partners — The entity assesses and manages risks associated with vendors and business partners.
desc.A: Availability — The Availability principle applies when availability of the system is included in the scope of engagement. It addresses capacity management, environmental protections, data backup, and recovery testing to ensure systems are available for operation and use as committed or agreed.
desc.A1: Availability Criteria — The three availability criteria cover current and future capacity management, environmental and infrastructure resilience, and the regular testing of recovery procedures.
desc.A1.1: Maintains, monitors, and evaluates processing capacity — The entity maintains, monitors, and evaluates current processing capacity and use of system components (infrastructure, data, and software) to manage capacity demand and to enable the implementation of additional capacity to help meet its objectives.
desc.A1.2: Maintains environmental protections, backups, and recovery infrastructure — The entity authorises, designs, develops or acquires, implements, operates, approves, maintains, and monitors environmental protections, software, data backup processes, and recovery infrastructure to meet its objectives.
desc.A1.3: Tests recovery plan procedures — The entity tests recovery plan procedures supporting system recovery to meet its objectives.
desc.PI: Processing Integrity — The Processing Integrity principle applies when complete, accurate, timely, and authorised processing is included in the scope of the engagement. It addresses whether system processing is valid, complete, and authorised from input through to output.
desc.PI1: Processing Integrity Criteria — The five processing integrity criteria address whether information is processed completely, validly, accurately, in a timely manner, and by authorised individuals or processes.
desc.PI1.1: Obtains and processes inputs completely, accurately, and timely — The entity obtains or generates, uses, and communicates relevant, quality information regarding the objectives related to processing, including definitions of data processed and product and service specifications.
desc.PI1.2: Processes inputs to achieve complete and accurate results — The entity implements policies and procedures over system inputs, including definitions of valid and invalid data inputs, to allow the system to process inputs correctly.
desc.PI1.3: Stores and maintains inputs and outputs completely and accurately — The entity stores and maintains the completeness, current status, and accuracy of system inputs, outputs, and the processing it performs.
desc.PI1.4: Outputs are complete, accurate, and distributed to authorised parties — The entity implements policies and procedures to make available or deliver output completely, accurately, and timely to meet the entity's objectives.
desc.PI1.5: Inputs and outputs are retained and protected — The entity implements policies and procedures to store inputs and resulting outputs to meet the entity's objectives.
desc.C: Confidentiality — The Confidentiality principle applies when the protection of confidential information is included in the scope of engagement. It addresses the identification and protection of confidential information throughout its lifecycle.
desc.C1: Confidentiality Criteria — The two confidentiality criteria address the identification and protection of confidential information, and the disposal of confidential information when it is no longer needed.
desc.C1.1: Identifies and maintains confidential information — The entity identifies and maintains confidential information to meet the entity's objectives related to confidentiality.
desc.C1.2: Disposes of confidential information — The entity disposes of confidential information to meet the entity's objectives related to confidentiality.
desc.P: Privacy — The Privacy principle applies when the collection, use, retention, disclosure, and disposal of personal information is included in the scope of the engagement. It addresses whether the entity handles personal information in conformity with its privacy notice and applicable privacy requirements.
desc.P1: Notice and Communication of Objectives — The notice criteria address whether the entity provides clear, accessible notice to data subjects about its privacy practices.
desc.P1.1: Provides notice to data subjects — The entity provides notice to data subjects about its privacy practices to meet the entity's objectives related to privacy. The notice is updated and communicated to data subjects in a timely manner for changes to the entity's privacy practices.
desc.P2: Choice and Consent — The choice and consent criteria address whether data subjects are given the opportunity to provide consent and make choices about the collection, use, and disclosure of their personal information.
desc.P2.1: Provides choices regarding collection, use, and disclosure — The entity communicates choices available regarding the collection, use, retention, disclosure, and disposal of personal information to the data subjects and the consequences, if any, of each choice.
desc.P3: Collection — The collection criteria address whether personal information is collected only for the purposes disclosed in the privacy notice and only when the entity has a valid lawful basis.
desc.P3.1: Collects personal information consistent with privacy notice — Personal information is collected consistent with the entity's objectives related to privacy.
desc.P3.2: Collects personal information only when consent or other lawful basis exists — The entity collects personal information only when a legal basis exists for doing so.
desc.P4: Use, Retention, and Disposal — The use, retention, and disposal criteria address whether personal information is used only for the purposes it was collected for, retained only as long as necessary, and disposed of securely.
desc.P4.1: Uses personal information for disclosed purposes — The entity limits the use of personal information to the purposes disclosed to data subjects.
desc.P4.2: Retains personal information only as long as necessary — The entity retains personal information consistent with the entity's objectives related to privacy.
desc.P4.3: Disposes of personal information securely — The entity disposes of personal information in a timely manner to meet the entity's objectives related to privacy.
desc.P5: Access — The access criteria address whether data subjects can access their personal information and correct inaccuracies.
desc.P5.1: Grants data subjects access to their personal information — The entity grants identified and authenticated data subjects the ability to access their stored personal information for review.
desc.P5.2: Corrects personal information upon request — The entity corrects or amends personal information based on a valid request by a data subject.
desc.P6: Disclosure to Third Parties — The disclosure criteria address whether personal information is disclosed to third parties only for disclosed purposes with appropriate protections in place.
desc.P6.1: Discloses personal information only for disclosed purposes — The entity discloses personal information to third parties with the consent of data subjects or as required by applicable law or regulation.
desc.P6.2: Creates and retains complete, accurate records of third-party disclosures — The entity creates and retains a complete and accurate record of authorized disclosures of personal information.
desc.P6.3: Informs data subjects of third-party disclosures — The entity provides notification of disclosures of personal information to third parties.
desc.P6.4: Discloses personal information only to service providers with equivalent privacy protections — The entity discloses personal information to third-party service providers only when the provider has agreed to implement the protections called for in the entity's privacy policies.
desc.P6.5: Notifies data subjects and authorities of privacy breaches — The entity notifies data subjects and, as required, authorities and others of a privacy breach or other event that could impact data subjects.
desc.P6.6: Addresses requests from data subjects and others regarding personal information — The entity addresses inquiries, complaints, and disputes from data subjects regarding personal information.
desc.P6.7: Provides accurate and complete personal information to third parties — The entity provides accurate and complete personal information to third parties when disclosure is authorized.
desc.P7: Quality — The quality criteria address whether personal information is accurate, complete, and relevant for the purposes it was collected.
desc.P7.1: Ensures accuracy and completeness of personal information — The entity collects and maintains accurate, up-to-date, complete, and relevant personal information to meet the entity's objectives related to privacy.
desc.P8: Monitoring and Enforcement — The monitoring and enforcement criteria address whether the entity monitors compliance with its privacy programme and enforces its privacy policies.
desc.P8.1: Monitors compliance with privacy policies and procedures — The entity monitors compliance with its privacy policies and procedures and has procedures to address privacy-related complaints and disputes.

about.title: About SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria
about.blurb: SOC 2 (System and Organisation Controls 2) is an auditing standard developed by the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants (AICPA). It evaluates service organisations against five Trust Services Criteria: Security (Common Criteria), Availability, Processing Integrity, Confidentiality, and Privacy. Unlike prescriptive standards, SOC 2 is principles-based — organisations define their own controls and auditors assess whether those controls meet the criteria. A SOC 2 Type II report covers a defined period (typically 6–12 months) and provides evidence of sustained operational effectiveness. It is widely required by enterprise customers as part of vendor due diligence.

sections.name: Common Criteria (Security)
sections.desc: The Security (Common Criteria) principle is mandatory for all SOC 2 engagements. It encompasses nine criteria covering the control environment, communication, risk assessment, monitoring, control activities, logical and physical access, system operations, change management, and risk mitigation.

sections.name: Availability
sections.desc: The Availability principle addresses whether systems are available for operation and use as committed or agreed. It covers capacity management, environmental protections, and recovery testing.

sections.name: Processing Integrity
sections.desc: The Processing Integrity principle addresses whether system processing is complete, valid, accurate, timely, and authorised to meet entity objectives.

sections.name: Confidentiality
sections.desc: The Confidentiality principle addresses whether information designated as confidential is protected as committed or agreed.

sections.name: Privacy
sections.desc: The Privacy principle addresses whether personal information is collected, used, retained, disclosed, and disposed of in conformity with the commitments in the entity's privacy notice and with criteria set by the AICPA.

groups.name: Common Criteria (Security)
groups.desc: The Common Criteria are required for all SOC 2 engagements and form the security foundation. They map directly to the COSO Internal Control — Integrated Framework and cover nine areas from governance through to risk mitigation.

sections.name: Control Environment
sections.desc: The Control Environment criteria assess whether the organisation demonstrates commitment to integrity and ethical values, maintains appropriate oversight structures, attracts and retains competent personnel, and enforces accountability for internal control responsibilities.

items.name: COSO Principle 1: Demonstrates commitment to integrity and ethical values
items.desc: The entity demonstrates a commitment to integrity and ethical values.
achieved: A formal Code of Conduct or Ethics Policy is documented, published, and communicated to all personnel
Annual acknowledgement of the Code of Conduct is tracked and completion rates meet or exceed the target threshold
Leadership visibly models ethical behaviour and security-conscious decision-making in documented forums (e.g., all-hands meetings, board minutes)
Whistleblowing or ethics reporting channels exist and are promoted across the organisation
Disciplinary procedures for violations of the Code of Conduct are documented and consistently applied
evidence: Signed Code of Conduct or Ethics Policy with version history and last-reviewed date
Employee acknowledgement completion report for the current review period
Board or senior leadership meeting minutes referencing ethics and integrity commitments
Whistleblowing policy and evidence of communication (e.g., intranet page, onboarding materials)

items.name: COSO Principle 2: Board exercises oversight responsibility
items.desc: The board of directors demonstrates independence from management and exercises oversight of the development and performance of internal control.
achieved: A board or equivalent governance body is formally constituted with independent members and documented terms of reference
Regular board or audit committee meetings are held with security and risk agenda items on record
The board reviews and approves the information security policy and programme at least annually
Board members with relevant expertise (e.g., cybersecurity, legal, finance) are identifiable in governance documentation
Escalation paths from management to the board for significant security incidents or control failures are defined
evidence: Board or audit committee charter and terms of reference
Meeting minutes from the past 12 months showing security and risk agenda items
Board-approved information security policy with sign-off dates
Governance structure diagram or organisational chart showing board composition

items.name: COSO Principle 3: Management establishes structures, reporting lines, and authorities
items.desc: Management establishes, with board oversight, structures, reporting lines, and appropriate authorities and responsibilities in the pursuit of objectives.
achieved: A documented organisational structure with clear reporting lines for security and risk functions is maintained and kept current
Role descriptions for security-relevant positions (CISO, Security Analyst, Risk Owner, Data Protection Officer) are formally documented
A RACI or responsibility matrix is maintained covering key security and compliance processes
Delegated authorities for security decisions (e.g., who can approve access, who can declare an incident) are formally defined
The structure is reviewed and updated whenever there are material organisational changes
evidence: Organisational chart showing security and risk function reporting lines
Role descriptions or job specifications for key security roles
RACI matrix for security processes such as incident response, change management, and access provisioning
Evidence of most recent review of the structure (e.g., HR records, policy review log)

items.name: COSO Principle 4: Demonstrates commitment to attract, develop, and retain competent individuals
items.desc: The entity demonstrates a commitment to attract, develop, and retain competent individuals in alignment with objectives.
achieved: Minimum security competency requirements are defined for roles with security responsibilities
Personnel in security roles hold or are actively working towards relevant professional qualifications or certifications
A training and development plan covering security skills is maintained for the security function
Succession planning or knowledge-transfer processes exist for critical security roles
Performance appraisals for security staff reference security-relevant competency objectives
evidence: Job descriptions with defined security competency requirements
Training records and professional certification evidence for security personnel
Annual training plan or personal development plans for the security team
Performance review documentation referencing security competencies

items.name: COSO Principle 5: Holds individuals accountable for internal control responsibilities
items.desc: The entity holds individuals accountable for their internal control responsibilities in the pursuit of objectives.
achieved: Security responsibilities are explicitly included in job descriptions and employment contracts
Performance objectives linked to security control ownership or compliance are set and tracked
A consequence management process exists for security policy violations and is consistently applied
Control owners formally accept accountability for assigned controls (e.g., via risk register sign-off)
Security KPIs or metrics are reported to management and tied to accountability frameworks
evidence: Employment contracts or role descriptions referencing security responsibilities
Performance management records showing security objectives and outcomes
Disciplinary records or case summaries (appropriately anonymised) demonstrating consistent enforcement
Control owner acceptance records from the risk register or GRC tool

sections.name: Communication and Information
sections.desc: The Communication and Information criteria assess whether the organisation generates, uses, and communicates relevant quality information both internally and externally to support the functioning of internal control.

items.name: COSO Principle 13: Uses relevant information to support internal control
items.desc: The entity obtains or generates and uses relevant, quality information to support the functioning of internal control.
achieved: An information classification scheme is defined and communicated across the organisation
Security-relevant data (logs, audit trails, vulnerability reports) is collected from systems and made available to those responsible for oversight
Dashboards or reporting mechanisms surface key security metrics to management on a regular cadence
Data quality checks are in place to ensure security reporting information is accurate and timely
Threat intelligence feeds are consumed and integrated into risk and security operations processes
evidence: Information classification policy with asset labelling guidance
Sample of a recurring security metrics or risk dashboard report
Evidence of threat intelligence subscription or feed integration (e.g., SIEM configuration, threat intel platform screenshots)
Data quality or audit log integrity reports

items.name: COSO Principle 14: Communicates internally to support internal control
items.desc: The entity internally communicates information, including objectives and responsibilities for internal control, necessary to support the functioning of internal control.
achieved: Security policies and procedures are published in a central, accessible location (e.g., intranet, policy management system) and version-controlled
All personnel complete mandatory security awareness training at onboarding and annually thereafter
Security bulletins, alerts, or newsletters are distributed to staff on a defined schedule
Internal communications reference security responsibilities and reinforce expected behaviours
Security incidents and lessons learned are communicated to relevant stakeholders after resolution
evidence: Policy management system or intranet page listing current security policies with version history
Security awareness training completion report for the current period
Sample of internal security communications (newsletters, bulletins, emails)
Post-incident communication or lessons-learned report shared internally

items.name: COSO Principle 15: Communicates externally
items.desc: The entity communicates with external parties regarding matters affecting the functioning of internal control.
achieved: A privacy notice or transparency statement is published and kept up to date for external data subjects
Contractual security requirements are communicated to vendors and third-party service providers
Processes exist for receiving and responding to external security disclosures (e.g., responsible disclosure or bug bounty programme)
Regulatory and customer security questionnaire responses are tracked and reviewed for accuracy
Communication protocols with regulators, law enforcement, and supervisory authorities are documented
evidence: Published privacy notice with last-updated date
Sample vendor contract or security addendum containing security obligations
Responsible disclosure policy or bug bounty programme documentation
Log of external security enquiries or questionnaire responses

sections.name: Risk Assessment
sections.desc: The Risk Assessment criteria assess whether the organisation specifies suitable objectives, identifies and analyses risks to achieving those objectives, assesses fraud risk, and identifies and assesses changes that could affect the system of internal control.

items.name: COSO Principle 6: Specifies suitable objectives
items.desc: The entity specifies objectives with sufficient clarity to enable the identification and assessment of risks relating to objectives.
achieved: Information security objectives are formally documented, aligned to business objectives, and approved by management
Security objectives are measurable and tracked against defined KPIs or targets
Objectives are reviewed at least annually and updated to reflect changes in the threat landscape or business strategy
The scope of risk assessments is clearly defined and aligned to the ISMS or SOC 2 service boundaries
Security objectives are communicated to relevant personnel and integrated into operational planning
evidence: Documented information security objectives with approval signatures and review dates
KPI or metric report tracking progress against security objectives
Management review minutes confirming objectives were discussed and validated
Risk assessment scope statement or terms of reference

items.name: COSO Principle 7: Identifies and analyses risk
items.desc: The entity identifies risks to the achievement of its objectives across the entity and analyses risks as a basis for determining how the risks should be managed.
achieved: A formal risk assessment methodology is documented and applied consistently across the in-scope system
A risk register is maintained, reviewed on a defined schedule, and includes likelihood, impact, and risk treatment decisions
Risk owners are assigned to each identified risk and are accountable for treatment actions
Risk assessments are triggered by significant changes (new technology, new services, incidents) as well as on a periodic schedule
Residual risk levels are assessed against an approved risk appetite statement
evidence: Risk assessment methodology document
Current risk register with risk owner assignments, likelihood/impact scores, and treatment plans
Risk appetite statement approved by senior management or the board
Evidence of risk reassessment triggered by a change event (e.g., new system launch)

items.name: COSO Principle 8: Assesses fraud risk
items.desc: The entity considers the potential for fraud in assessing risks to the achievement of objectives.
achieved: Fraud risk is explicitly included as a category within the risk assessment process
Anti-fraud controls (e.g., segregation of duties, reconciliations, audit trails) are identified and mapped to fraud risk scenarios
Management assesses the risk of management override of controls as part of the fraud risk assessment
Fraud awareness is included in the security awareness training programme
Whistleblowing mechanisms are in place and communicated as a fraud-reporting channel
evidence: Risk register or risk assessment output showing fraud risk entries
