sections.name: Security Updates
sections.desc: Devices, software, and operating systems are kept up to date to address known security vulnerabilities.

groups.name: Firewalls
groups.desc: The Firewalls theme requires organisations to protect all devices that can be connected to the internet, whether directly or via a home or public network, using boundary firewalls and internet gateways. All devices must have a software firewall or host-based firewall enabled. The default firewall configuration must block all traffic that has not been explicitly permitted, and rules must be documented and reviewed regularly. Unapproved services must not be exposed to the internet.
achieved: A boundary firewall or equivalent network security control is in place at every connection point between the organisation's network and the internet
All organisation-managed devices have a host-based software firewall enabled, blocking all inbound connections not explicitly required
Firewall rules are documented with a business justification for each permitted rule, and unapproved services are not exposed
Default administrative passwords on all firewalls and routers have been changed to strong, unique credentials
Firewall rule sets are reviewed at least every 12 months and whenever a significant network change is made
evidence: Network diagram showing firewall placement at all internet-facing boundaries
Firewall rule set documentation with business justification for each permitted rule and most recent review date
Host-based firewall configuration screenshots or management console reports showing enabled status on all managed devices
Evidence that administrative credentials on firewalls have been changed from vendor defaults (e.g., password management system entries)

items.name: Boundary firewall protection at all internet connections
items.desc: A boundary firewall or equivalent control is deployed at every connection between the organisation's internal network and the internet, ensuring all traffic passes through an approved security control point.
achieved: All internet connections pass through a firewall or equivalent NSC before reaching internal devices
Cloud-hosted assets are protected by cloud security groups or equivalent controls configured to the same standards
Network topology diagrams are maintained showing all internet connection points and associated firewall positions
Perimeter firewalls are patched and maintained in accordance with the Security Updates theme
evidence: Current network diagram showing all internet connection points and firewall positions
Cloud security group or NSC configuration export for cloud-hosted assets
Firewall patch level and maintenance records

items.name: Firewall rule documentation and review
items.desc: All firewall rules permitting traffic are documented with a clear business justification, and the rule set is reviewed at least annually to remove rules that are no longer required.
achieved: Every firewall rule that permits inbound or outbound traffic has a documented business justification
Rule sets are reviewed and validated by an authorised person at least every 12 months
Rules that are no longer required are removed or disabled promptly following the review
A change management process governs the addition of new firewall rules
evidence: Firewall rule documentation with justification for each permitted rule
Annual rule review sign-off record showing review date and reviewer identity
Change management records for firewall rule additions or modifications

items.name: Host-based software firewall on all devices
items.desc: A software firewall is enabled on all organisation-managed devices, blocking all inbound connections that have not been explicitly permitted.
achieved: Host-based firewall or equivalent endpoint protection is enabled on all managed endpoints (desktops, laptops, servers)
The default inbound rule is to block all connections unless explicitly permitted
Users are prevented from disabling the host-based firewall without administrative approval
Mobile devices used for work purposes have equivalent protection via MDM-enforced firewall policies
evidence: Endpoint management tool (MDM/EPP) report showing firewall status across all managed devices
Group Policy or MDM policy configuration preventing user disablement of the firewall
Mobile device management policy configuration for work mobile devices

groups.name: Secure Configuration
groups.desc: The Secure Configuration theme requires that all organisation-managed computers and network devices are configured to reduce the attack surface. Unnecessary software, services, and user accounts must be removed or disabled. Vendor-supplied default passwords must be changed before devices are put into use. Only approved and necessary software should be installed on devices, and auto-run features that automatically execute code from removable media should be disabled.
achieved: All devices are configured using documented secure configuration standards before being put into use
Default usernames and passwords on all devices and software are changed before deployment
Unnecessary user accounts (including default accounts) are disabled or removed
Unnecessary software, services, and protocols are uninstalled or disabled on all devices
Auto-run and auto-play features are disabled on all devices to prevent malicious code execution from removable media
evidence: Secure configuration standards or hardening guides for each device type managed by the organisation
Evidence that default credentials have been changed (password manager records, device configuration screenshots)
Device build record or MDM configuration profile showing unnecessary services are disabled
Group Policy or MDM policy evidence showing auto-run is disabled

items.name: Default password changes on all devices and software
items.desc: Vendor-supplied default passwords on all internet-connected devices, accounts, and software are changed to unique, strong passwords before the device or software is put into use.
achieved: A documented process requires default passwords to be changed before any device or software is deployed
A password management solution or policy ensures strong, unique credentials are set
Default accounts that cannot be removed are renamed or disabled where the operating system permits
Verification that defaults have been changed is part of the device build acceptance process
evidence: Device deployment procedure referencing default credential changes
Password management system entries for device administrative credentials
Build acceptance checklist including default credential verification step

items.name: Disable unnecessary services and open ports
items.desc: All services, protocols, and open network ports that are not required for the device's function are disabled or removed to reduce the attack surface.
achieved: Hardening standards define which services and ports should be enabled for each device role
Devices are audited against hardening standards before and after deployment
Vulnerability scanning identifies services and open ports that deviate from the hardening baseline
Services that were not required but found enabled are disabled within a defined remediation timeframe
evidence: Hardening standards for each device type showing permitted and prohibited services
Vulnerability or port scan results confirming compliance with hardening standards
Remediation records for any deviations found during audits

items.name: Restrict software installation to authorised software only
items.desc: Users are prevented from installing software that has not been approved by the organisation, and a process exists to manage and review what software is installed across the estate.
achieved: Users do not have local administrative rights that would allow arbitrary software installation
An approved software list is maintained and communicated to users
Technical controls (application allow-listing, MDM restrictions) prevent installation of unapproved software
The software inventory is reviewed periodically and unauthorised software is removed
evidence: MDM or Group Policy configuration preventing standard users from installing software
Approved software list with review date
Software inventory report with any unauthorised software flagged and remediated
Application control or allow-listing configuration

groups.name: Access Control
groups.desc: The Access Control theme requires that user accounts are created and maintained on the basis of least privilege, with access limited to what is needed for the user's role. Administrative accounts must be used only for administrative tasks and must be separate from standard user accounts. Multi-factor authentication must be enabled for all accounts that can access cloud services, administrator accounts, and accounts accessing data or services exposed to the internet. Unused accounts must be removed or disabled promptly.
achieved: User accounts are created only when there is a business need and are assigned only the privileges required for the user's role
Administrative accounts are separate from standard user accounts and are used exclusively for administrative tasks
Multi-factor authentication is enabled for all cloud service accounts, all administrative accounts, and all accounts with internet-facing access to organisation data
User accounts are reviewed at least every 12 months and accounts that are no longer required are removed or disabled
All account creation, modification, and removal is authorised and documented
evidence: User account management procedure covering creation, modification, and removal
Annual user access review report with evidence of accounts removed or disabled as a result
MFA configuration evidence for cloud services, administrative accounts, and internet-facing applications
Joiner–mover–leaver procedure and sample evidence of timely de-provisioning

items.name: User account management and least privilege
items.desc: User accounts are created with only the privileges needed for the individual's role, and privilege is reviewed and adjusted when roles change.
achieved: A documented process exists for creating, modifying, and disabling user accounts based on role requirements
Access requests are reviewed and approved by a manager or account owner before access is granted
Access rights are reviewed when a user changes role and unnecessary privileges are removed
A user access review is completed at least annually
evidence: Access provisioning procedure
Sample access request tickets showing manager approval
User access review report from the most recent review cycle
Evidence of access adjustment on role changes (e.g., tickets, provisioning system logs)

items.name: Multi-factor authentication for all applicable accounts
items.desc: Multi-factor authentication is enabled for all user and administrator accounts that access cloud services, administrator interfaces, and internet-facing data or services.
achieved: MFA is enforced for all Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, or equivalent cloud service accounts
MFA is enforced for all accounts with access to administrative interfaces (servers, routers, firewalls, management consoles)
MFA is enforced for all accounts that can access organisation data via internet-facing applications
MFA cannot be bypassed by users or disabled without authorised approval
MFA method used meets the NCSC strength guidance (app-based authentication preferred over SMS)
evidence: Identity provider or cloud console MFA enforcement configuration screenshots
MFA coverage report showing percentage of accounts with MFA enabled
MFA policy documentation specifying required methods and exclusion approval process

items.name: Separate administrative accounts
items.desc: Administrative privileges are used only via dedicated administrative accounts, separate from the user's standard day-to-day account, and used only for administrative tasks.
achieved: All users who require administrative access have a separate, dedicated administrative account
Administrative accounts are not used for everyday activities such as email, web browsing, or accessing non-administrative applications
The use of administrative accounts is logged and monitored for suspicious activity
Administrative account credentials are held securely, ideally in a privileged access management (PAM) solution
evidence: Account management procedure requiring separate administrative accounts
Active Directory, Azure AD, or equivalent report showing administrative account separation
Audit log evidence of administrative account usage patterns
PAM solution configuration or password management records for administrative credentials

items.name: Prompt removal of unused accounts
items.desc: User accounts that are no longer required (for example, because a user has left the organisation or a service has been decommissioned) are removed or disabled promptly.
achieved: A leaver process ensures accounts are disabled within 24 hours of departure for standard users and immediately for privileged accounts
Regular account audits identify stale or unused accounts that have not been deactivated via the leaver process
Service and shared accounts are reviewed periodically and disabled or removed when no longer needed
Account disablement is logged and the log is retained for audit purposes
evidence: Leaver process documentation showing account disablement timelines
Sample leaver tickets showing timely account disablement
Stale account audit report with remediation evidence
Account disablement audit log extracts

groups.name: Malware Protection
groups.desc: The Malware Protection theme requires that organisation-managed devices are protected against malware using one or more of: anti-malware software, application allow-listing, or sandboxing. Anti-malware software must be kept up to date, must be actively running, and must perform regular scans or real-time protection. Devices that are not covered by anti-malware must be covered by application allow-listing as an alternative approach, which the NCSC considers equally or more effective.
achieved: All devices are protected against malware using anti-malware software with real-time protection enabled, application allow-listing, or equivalent sandboxing controls
Anti-malware signature definitions are updated automatically and at least daily
Anti-malware software is actively running on all protected devices and the protection cannot be disabled by the user
Email and web filtering controls reduce the risk of malware delivery via the most common attack vectors
The malware protection approach is documented, maintained, and reviewed at least annually
evidence: Anti-malware deployment report showing coverage and active status across all managed devices
Anti-malware update configuration showing automatic daily updates
Email filtering and web filtering configuration evidence
Malware protection policy and most recent annual review record

items.name: Anti-malware software deployed and actively running
items.desc: Anti-malware or endpoint detection and response software is deployed on all organisation-managed devices, is running with real-time protection enabled, and is configured to prevent users from disabling it.
achieved: Anti-malware software with real-time scanning is installed and running on all managed endpoints
Users cannot disable or uninstall anti-malware software without administrative credentials
The anti-malware console provides visibility into the protection status of all managed devices
Devices that are offline or have out-of-date protection are identified and remediated
evidence: Anti-malware management console report showing real-time protection status across the device estate
Policy configuration preventing user disablement of anti-malware
Report identifying devices with protection gaps and remediation records

items.name: Web filtering to block access to malicious sites
items.desc: Web content filtering is in place to prevent users from accessing known malicious websites and to reduce the risk of malware delivery via web browsing.
achieved: DNS or proxy-based web filtering blocks access to known malicious domains and categories
Web filtering covers all devices, including those accessing the internet from home or public networks (via VPN, DNS-based filtering, or browser extensions)
Web filtering logs are reviewed for suspicious access patterns
The filtering policy is reviewed and updated at least annually
evidence: Web filtering configuration and category block list
Coverage evidence showing filtering applies to remote and office-based devices equally
Sample web filtering log review records
Annual web filtering policy review record

items.name: Application allow-listing as an alternative or supplementary control
items.desc: Where anti-malware software is not deployed, or as a supplementary control, application allow-listing is implemented to prevent the execution of unapproved software on devices.
achieved: An approved application list is maintained for device types covered by allow-listing
Allow-listing controls are enforced through technical means (e.g., AppLocker, Windows Defender Application Control, MDM restrictions)
Users cannot run applications not on the approved list without explicit authorisation
The approved application list is reviewed at least annually and updated when new software is needed
evidence: Application allow-listing policy or approved software list
Technical control configuration (e.g., AppLocker policy, WDAC policy)
Evidence that unapproved applications are blocked (e.g., block event logs)
Annual approved application list review record

groups.name: Security Updates
groups.desc: The Security Updates theme requires that all software, operating systems, and firmware on in-scope devices are kept up to date to address known security vulnerabilities. High and critical severity patches must be applied within 14 days of release. Software that is no longer supported by the vendor (end-of-life or end-of-support) and that cannot be patched must be removed from the scope of the Cyber Essentials assessment or protected by compensating controls. Automatic updates should be enabled where possible.
achieved: All in-scope operating systems, software, and firmware receive security updates within 14 days of release for high and critical severity patches
Automatic updates are enabled for all software where this option is available
A patch management process is documented, covering discovery, prioritisation, deployment, and verification of patches
Unsupported or end-of-life software is removed from in-scope devices or is subject to risk acceptance with documented compensating controls
The patch status of all in-scope devices is monitored and devices with missing patches are remediated within the required timeframe
evidence: Patch management policy defining the 14-day SLA for high and critical patches
Vulnerability scan or patch management tool report showing patch compliance across all in-scope devices
Evidence of auto-update configuration on operating systems and key software
Software inventory identifying any end-of-life or unsupported software with risk acceptance records or removal evidence

items.name: 14-day patching SLA for high and critical vulnerabilities
items.desc: Security patches rated high or critical severity are applied to all in-scope devices within 14 days of the patch becoming available from the vendor.
achieved: A patch management process identifies new high and critical patches within 24 hours of release
Patches are tested and deployed within the 14-day SLA; where testing delays are unavoidable, a documented exception process is followed
Compliance with the 14-day SLA is tracked and reported to management
Emergency patching procedures allow out-of-band deployment for critical patches when the standard cycle cannot meet the SLA
evidence: Patch management procedure specifying the 14-day SLA and emergency patching process
Patch compliance report showing application dates relative to release dates for high and critical patches
Exception records for any patches not applied within SLA, with risk acceptance
Management reporting on patch compliance KPIs

items.name: Operating system, firmware, and application updates applied
items.desc: Security updates are applied to all in-scope software categories: operating systems, firmware (BIOS, UEFI, network device firmware), and third-party applications.
achieved: Operating system updates are managed centrally and deployed within the required timeframe
Network device and server firmware updates are tracked and applied when security patches are released
Third-party application updates (browsers, office suites, productivity tools) are managed and applied promptly
A software and firmware inventory enables complete visibility of what needs to be patched
evidence: OS patch management tool report (e.g., WSUS, SCCM, Intune) showing OS patch status
Network device and firmware inventory with current version levels and available patch versions
Third-party application update management configuration and compliance report
Software and firmware asset inventory

items.name: Unsupported software removed or risk-accepted
items.desc: Software, operating systems, and firmware that are no longer supported by the vendor and no longer receive security updates are removed from in-scope devices. Where removal is not possible, a formal risk acceptance is documented and compensating controls are applied.
achieved: A software inventory identifies the support status and end-of-life dates for all installed software and OS versions
End-of-life software is removed from in-scope devices before or immediately upon reaching end of support
Where removal is not possible prior to assessment, a formal risk acceptance is documented with details of compensating controls applied
A process exists to proactively plan migrations away from software approaching end of life
evidence: Software inventory with vendor-stated support end dates
Evidence of end-of-life software removal (e.g., before/after software inventory comparison)
Risk acceptance records for any end-of-life software retained, with compensating control documentation
Migration plan for software approaching end of life

desc.AC: Access Control — Policies and procedures for system access, account management, least privilege, remote access, and wireless access. Covers the full spectrum of who can access what resources and under what conditions.
desc.AT: Awareness and Training — Ensures that personnel are aware of the security risks associated with their activities and are trained to carry out their assigned security responsibilities.
desc.AU: Audit and Accountability — Creates, protects, retains, and reviews system audit records to enable monitoring, analysis, investigation, and reporting of unlawful or unauthorised system activity.
desc.CA: Assessment, Authorisation, and Monitoring — Assesses security and privacy controls, authorises system operation, monitors controls on an ongoing basis, and conducts penetration testing and security assessments.
desc.CM: Configuration Management — Establishes and maintains the integrity of information systems by using a configuration management and change control process for hardware, software, firmware, and documentation.
desc.CP: Contingency Planning — Establishes, maintains, and effectively implements plans for emergency response, backup operations, and post-disaster recovery for systems to ensure the availability of critical resources and continuity of operations.
desc.IA: Identification and Authentication — Identifies information system users, processes acting on behalf of users, and devices, and authenticates the identities of those users, processes, or devices as a prerequisite to allowing access.
desc.IR: Incident Response — Establishes an operational incident handling capability for information system security incidents that includes preparation, detection, analysis, containment, recovery, and user response activities.
desc.MA: Maintenance — Performs maintenance on information systems, including controls on the tools, techniques, mechanisms, and personnel that conduct system maintenance.
desc.MP: Media Protection — Protects system media, both digital and non-digital, limits access to information on system media to authorised users, and sanitises or destroys media before disposal or reuse.
desc.PE: Physical and Environmental Protection — Limits physical access to information systems, equipment, and the respective operating environments to authorised individuals, and protects systems from environmental hazards.
desc.PL: Planning — Develops, documents, and periodically updates security and privacy plans for information systems that describe the security controls in place and the rules of behaviour for individuals accessing the systems.
desc.PM: Programme Management — Enterprise-wide programme management controls that support the implementation of the risk management framework — including security governance, risk management strategy, insider threat programme, and security workforce management.
desc.PS: Personnel Security — Ensures that individuals occupying positions of responsibility within organisations are trustworthy and meet established security criteria, and that systems are protected during and after personnel actions such as terminations and transfers.
desc.PT: Personally Identifiable Information Processing and Transparency — Addresses the processing of personally identifiable information (PII), including consent and privacy notices, the minimisation of PII collection, and the rights of individuals with respect to their PII.
desc.RA: Risk Assessment — Assesses the risk to organisational operations, assets, individuals, and other organisations resulting from the operation of information systems and the processing of information.
desc.SA: System and Services Acquisition — Allocates sufficient resources to protect information systems, employs system development life cycle processes that incorporate information security, applies developer configuration management, and ensures appropriate security considerations in supply chain risk management.
desc.SC: System and Communications Protection — Monitors, controls, and protects communications at the external boundaries and key internal boundaries of information systems, and employs architectural designs, software development techniques, and systems engineering principles that promote security.
desc.SI: System and Information Integrity — Identifies, reports, and corrects information system flaws, provides protection from malicious code, monitors alerts and advisories, and verifies the correct operation of security functions.
desc.SR: Supply Chain Risk Management — Establishes a supply chain risk management strategy, identifies and assesses supply chain risks, and implements controls to address those risks throughout the system development life cycle.

about.title: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5
about.blurb: NIST Special Publication 800-53 provides a catalogue of security and privacy controls for information systems and organisations. Revision 5 reorganised controls into 20 families, made them outcome-based, and integrated privacy controls alongside security controls. It is widely used as the baseline for US federal systems and referenced globally.

p: Controls are organised into 20 families identified by two-letter identifiers (e.g. AC for Access Control). Each family contains a set of numbered controls and control enhancements.

NIST SP 800-53B defines three control baselines — Low, Moderate, and High — corresponding to the impact level of the information system. Organisations select and tailor controls from the appropriate baseline.

groups.name: Access Control
groups.desc: Policies and procedures for system access, account management, least privilege, remote access, and wireless access. Covers the full spectrum of who can access what resources and under what conditions.
achieved: An Access Control policy is established, documented, approved, and reviewed at defined intervals.
Account management procedures are implemented covering provisioning, modification, disabling, removal, and review.
Least privilege is enforced; users have only the access required for their assigned roles.
Remote access is controlled, monitored, and requires multi-factor authentication.
Separation of duties is implemented to reduce the risk of malicious activity.
evidence: Access Control Policy document (AC-1) with approval and review history
Account management procedure and quarterly user access review records (AC-2)
Least-privilege configuration evidence and role-based access reports (AC-6)
Remote access policy and MFA configuration evidence (AC-17)

groups.name: Awareness and Training
groups.desc: Ensures that personnel are aware of the security risks associated with their activities and are trained to carry out their assigned security responsibilities.
achieved: All personnel complete security awareness training before system access and annually thereafter.
Individuals with security responsibilities receive role-specific training.
Training records are maintained and used to track completion.
Training content is reviewed and updated at least annually.
evidence: Security awareness training completion records for all personnel (AT-2)
Role-specific security training records for privileged users and system administrators (AT-3)
Training programme documentation with annual review evidence (AT-1)

groups.name: Audit and Accountability
groups.desc: Creates, protects, retains, and reviews system audit records to enable monitoring, analysis, investigation, and reporting of unlawful or unauthorised system activity.
achieved: Audit logging is enabled for all in-scope systems capturing required event types.
Audit records are protected from unauthorised access, modification, and deletion.
Log retention meets defined requirements (minimum 90 days online, 12 months archived).
Audit records are reviewed at least weekly for anomalies and potential incidents.
System clocks are synchronised to authoritative time sources.
evidence: Audit log configuration showing enabled event types per system (AU-2, AU-12)
SIEM centralised logging evidence with log protection configuration (AU-9)
Log retention policy and storage configuration (AU-11)
Weekly audit review records or automated review evidence (AU-6)

groups.name: Assessment, Authorisation, and Monitoring
groups.desc: Assesses security and privacy controls, authorises system operation, monitors controls on an ongoing basis, and conducts penetration testing and security assessments.
achieved: Security assessments are conducted at defined intervals and when significant changes occur.
Systems operate under an authorisation to operate (ATO) based on accepted risk.
Plan of action and milestones (POA&M) tracks identified weaknesses to remediation.
Continuous monitoring programme is in place covering all controls.
evidence: Security assessment report (SAR) and plan of action and milestones (CA-2, CA-5)
Authorisation to operate (ATO) documentation (CA-6)
Continuous monitoring strategy and evidence of ongoing assessment activities (CA-7)
Penetration testing records (CA-8)

groups.name: Configuration Management
groups.desc: Establishes and maintains the integrity of information systems by using a configuration management and change control process for hardware, software, firmware, and documentation.
achieved: Security configuration baselines are established and documented for all system types.
Configuration changes go through a formal change control process with security impact analysis.
Unauthorised changes to system configurations are detected and remediated.
Software installation on operational systems is restricted to authorised software only.
evidence: Security configuration baseline documents (CIS Benchmarks or equivalent) (CM-6)
Change management policy and change approval records (CM-3)
Configuration monitoring scan reports showing baseline compliance (CM-6)
Approved software list and installation control evidence (CM-7, CM-11)

groups.name: Contingency Planning
groups.desc: Establishes, maintains, and effectively implements plans for emergency response, backup operations, and post-disaster recovery for systems to ensure the availability of critical resources and continuity of operations.
achieved: A contingency plan is developed, tested, and updated at least annually.
Backups of system data and software are performed and protected.
Recovery objectives (RTO/RPO) are defined and met through redundancy and backup strategies.
Contingency plan exercises are conducted at least annually.
evidence: Contingency plan document with approval and last update date (CP-2)
Backup schedule, completion logs, and restore test records (CP-9)
Annual contingency plan exercise report with lessons learned (CP-4)
Alternate processing and storage site documentation (CP-7, CP-8)

groups.name: Identification and Authentication
groups.desc: Identifies information system users, processes acting on behalf of users, and devices, and authenticates the identities of those users, processes, or devices as a prerequisite to allowing access.
achieved: All users are uniquely identified — shared or generic accounts are prohibited.
Multi-factor authentication is enforced for privileged accounts and remote access.
Passwords or authenticators meet defined strength and lifecycle requirements.
Service and device identities are managed through a formal process.
evidence: Identity and authentication policy and unique user ID verification (IA-2, IA-4)
MFA enforcement configuration and coverage report for privileged accounts (IA-2(1))
Password policy configuration showing strength and expiry settings (IA-5)
Service account and device identity inventory (IA-3)

groups.name: Incident Response
groups.desc: Establishes an operational incident handling capability for information system security incidents that includes preparation, detection, analysis, containment, recovery, and user response activities.
achieved: An incident response plan is documented covering all phases from preparation to lessons learned.
Incident response team roles and escalation paths are defined and communicated.
Incidents are detected, classified, and responded to within defined timeframes.
Post-incident reviews are conducted and drive improvements to controls and the IRP.
evidence: Incident response plan document with approval and review history (IR-8)
Incident response team RACI and contact list (IR-2)
Incident tracking records showing classification, response, and closure times (IR-5)
Post-incident review reports with follow-up action tracking (IR-4)

groups.name: Maintenance
groups.desc: Performs maintenance on information systems, including controls on the tools, techniques, mechanisms, and personnel that conduct system maintenance.
achieved: System maintenance is performed by authorised personnel only.
Maintenance activities are logged with details of work performed.
Equipment sent off-site for maintenance is sanitised of sensitive data.
Remote maintenance sessions are monitored and terminated when complete.
evidence: Maintenance authorisation records and personnel vetting evidence (MA-2, MA-5)
Maintenance logs with timestamps, personnel, and work performed (MA-2)
Remote maintenance session monitoring configuration and logs (MA-4)
Media sanitisation records for equipment sent for off-site maintenance (MA-3)

groups.name: Media Protection
groups.desc: Protects system media, both digital and non-digital, limits access to information on system media to authorised users, and sanitises or destroys media before disposal or reuse.
achieved: Access to system media is restricted to authorised personnel.
Media containing sensitive information is marked, protected, and tracked.
Media is sanitised or destroyed in accordance with approved procedures before disposal or reuse.
Media transport is protected using encryption or physical safeguards.
evidence: Media access control configuration and inventory of sensitive media (MP-2, MP-3)
Media sanitisation procedures and destruction records (MP-6)
Media transport policy and encryption configuration for transportable media (MP-5)
Certificates of destruction from approved media disposal provider (MP-6)

groups.name: Physical and Environmental Protection
groups.desc: Limits physical access to information systems, equipment, and the respective operating environments to authorised individuals, and protects systems from environmental hazards.
achieved: Physical access to facilities and systems is controlled and limited to authorised personnel.
Access logs and CCTV records are maintained and reviewed.
Environmental controls (fire, flood, temperature, power) protect information processing facilities.
Visitors are escorted and logged in controlled areas.
evidence: Physical access control configuration and quarterly access review records (PE-2, PE-3)
CCTV coverage documentation and footage retention policy (PE-6)
Environmental monitoring system configuration and alert records (PE-14)
Visitor log records and escort procedure documentation (PE-8)

groups.name: Planning
groups.desc: Develops, documents, and periodically updates security and privacy plans for information systems that describe the security controls in place and the rules of behaviour for individuals accessing the systems.
achieved: A system security plan (SSP) is developed, maintained, and reviewed at defined intervals.
Rules of behaviour (acceptable use) are defined and acknowledged by all users.
Security planning processes address the overall strategy for protecting systems.
Privacy plans are developed where personally identifiable information is processed.
evidence: System Security Plan (SSP) with approval and last update evidence (PL-2)
Acceptable Use Policy (Rules of Behaviour) with signed acknowledgements (PL-4)
Security and privacy planning process documentation (PL-1)

groups.name: Programme Management
groups.desc: Enterprise-wide programme management controls that support the implementation of the risk management framework — including security governance, risk management strategy, insider threat programme, and security workforce management.
achieved: An enterprise-wide information security programme is established with senior management accountability.
Risk management strategy and tolerance levels are defined and communicated.
An insider threat programme is established to detect and respond to insider risk.
Security resources are allocated commensurate with identified risks.
evidence: Information Security Programme Plan (PM-1)
Risk management strategy document with risk tolerance thresholds (PM-9)
Insider threat programme documentation and monitoring evidence (PM-12)
Information security workforce and training plan (PM-13)

groups.name: Personnel Security
groups.desc: Ensures that individuals occupying positions of responsibility within organisations are trustworthy and meet established security criteria, and that systems are protected during and after personnel actions such as terminations and transfers.
achieved: Personnel are screened before being granted access to systems and data.
Position risk designations are established for all positions.
Access is terminated promptly upon personnel separation.
Personnel security requirements are included in agreements with third-party providers.
evidence: Pre-employment screening policy and records (PS-3)
Position risk designation register (PS-2)
Offboarding checklist showing timely access revocation on separation (PS-4)
Third-party personnel security clauses in contracts (PS-7)

groups.name: Personally Identifiable Information Processing and Transparency
groups.desc: Addresses the processing of personally identifiable information (PII), including consent and privacy notices, the minimisation of PII collection, and the rights of individuals with respect to their PII.
achieved: Privacy notices are provided to individuals at the point of PII collection.
PII is minimised to only that which is necessary for the stated purpose.
Consent records are maintained where consent is the legal basis for processing.
Individual access and correction rights are supported through defined procedures.
evidence: Privacy notice documentation and publication evidence (PT-5)
Data minimisation policy and privacy impact assessment records (PT-2, PT-3)
Consent management records (PT-4)
Data subject rights procedure and request handling records (PT-6)

groups.name: Risk Assessment
groups.desc: Assesses the risk to organisational operations, assets, individuals, and other organisations resulting from the operation of information systems and the processing of information.
achieved: Risk assessments are conducted at defined intervals and when significant changes occur.

desc.Art.21(a): Policies on risk analysis and information system security — Article 21(2)(a) requires entities to have policies on risk analysis and information system security. Entities must establish, document, implement, and maintain policies that address risk identification, assessment, treatment, and the security of networks and information systems used in the provision of their services.
desc.Art.21(b): Incident handling — Article 21(2)(b) requires entities to have incident handling procedures. This encompasses detection, analysis, containment, notification, and recovery from security incidents affecting networks and information systems.
desc.Art.21(c): Business continuity, such as backup management and disaster recovery, and crisis management — Article 21(2)(c) requires entities to have business continuity measures including backup management, disaster recovery, and crisis management arrangements to ensure the continued provision of services and rapid recovery from disruption.
desc.Art.21(d): Supply chain security, including security-related aspects concerning the relationships between each entity and its direct suppliers or service providers — Article 21(2)(d) requires entities to address supply chain security, including the cybersecurity practices of direct suppliers and service providers and the contractual security requirements governing those relationships.
desc.Art.21(e): Security in network and information systems acquisition, development and maintenance, including vulnerability handling and disclosure — Article 21(2)(e) requires security to be embedded throughout the acquisition, development, and maintenance lifecycle of networks and information systems, including processes for vulnerability handling and responsible disclosure.
desc.Art.21(f): Policies and procedures to assess the effectiveness of cybersecurity risk-management measures — Article 21(2)(f) requires entities to have policies and procedures to assess the effectiveness of their cybersecurity risk management measures. This includes monitoring, measurement, review, and audit activities to verify that controls are working as intended.
desc.Art.21(g): Basic cyber hygiene practices and cybersecurity training — Article 21(2)(g) requires entities to implement basic cyber hygiene practices and cybersecurity training for their personnel. Cyber hygiene covers fundamental practices including patching, access control, MFA, and secure configuration.
desc.Art.21(h): Policies and procedures regarding the use of cryptography and, where appropriate, encryption — Article 21(2)(h) requires entities to have policies and procedures governing the use of cryptography and encryption. This includes the selection of algorithms, key management, and the protection of data at rest and in transit.
desc.Art.21(i): Human resources security, access control policies and asset management — Article 21(2)(i) requires entities to address human resources security, access control, and asset management. This encompasses personnel security measures throughout the employment lifecycle, logical and physical access controls, and the management of information assets.
desc.Art.21(j): The use of multi-factor authentication or continuous authentication solutions, secured voice, video and text communications, and secured emergency communication systems — Article 21(2)(j) requires entities to use multi-factor authentication (MFA) or continuous authentication solutions, and to use secure communications systems. This reflects the critical importance of strong authentication and encrypted communications in preventing account compromise and eavesdropping.

about.title: NIS 2 Directive — Article 21 Security Measures
about.blurb: The Network and Information Security Directive 2 (NIS 2) requires essential and important entities to implement appropriate technical, operational, and organisational measures to manage cybersecurity risks. Article 21(2) specifies ten minimum measures. Member States were required to transpose NIS 2 by 17 October 2024.

p: NIS 2 applies to 'essential' entities (large organisations in critical sectors such as energy, transport, health, finance, water, digital infrastructure) and 'important' entities (medium-sized organisations in additional sectors). The Directive establishes a proportionality requirement — measures must be appropriate to the risk and the size of the entity.

Article 21(2) lists ten specific cybersecurity measures that entities must implement as a minimum. These are supplemented by implementing acts specifying technical and methodological requirements for certain sectors.

groups.name: Policies on risk analysis and information system security
groups.desc: Article 21(2)(a) requires entities to have policies on risk analysis and information system security. Entities must establish, document, implement, and maintain policies that address risk identification, assessment, treatment, and the security of networks and information systems used in the provision of their services.

desc.Cl.4: Context of the Organisation — Clause 4 requires the organisation to understand its context — internal and external issues, interested parties and their requirements, and the scope of the BCMS — before implementing continuity plans.
desc.Cl.5: Leadership — Clause 5 requires top management to demonstrate commitment to the BCMS through defined leadership behaviours, establishing a business continuity policy, and assigning roles and responsibilities.
desc.Cl.6: Planning — Clause 6 requires the organisation to determine the actions needed to address risks and opportunities, set BCMS objectives, and plan how to achieve them.
desc.Cl.7: Support — Clause 7 covers the supporting elements of the BCMS — resources, competence, awareness, communication, and documented information — that enable effective implementation.
desc.Cl.8: Operation — Clause 8 covers the operational requirements of the BCMS — business impact analysis, risk assessment, business continuity strategy, plans, recovery procedures, and exercising. This is where the practical BC capability is built and verified.
desc.Cl.8.2: Business Impact Analysis — The organisation shall establish, implement, and maintain a formal process to determine the impact of disruptive incidents over time. The BIA identifies time-critical activities, recovery time objectives, recovery point objectives, resource requirements, and dependencies.
desc.Cl.8.3: Business Continuity Strategy — Based on the BIA and risk assessment outputs, the organisation shall determine appropriate continuity strategies for protecting prioritised activities, stabilising and continuing those activities, and recovering and restoring them following disruption.
desc.Cl.8.4: Business Continuity Plans and Procedures — The organisation shall document procedures that enable it to manage a disruptive incident and continue critical activities at the required level. Plans must include incident response procedures, activation criteria, communication procedures, and resource management.
desc.Cl.8.5: Recovery — The organisation shall have documented procedures for recovering critical activities following a disruption, returning to normal operations, and restoring systems and data within defined recovery objectives.
desc.Cl.8.6: Exercising and Testing — The organisation shall exercise and test its business continuity procedures to ensure they are consistent with its business continuity objectives, with exercises conducted at planned intervals and after significant changes.
desc.Cl.9: Performance Evaluation — Clause 9 requires the organisation to monitor, measure, analyse, and evaluate its BCMS to ensure it remains effective, and to conduct internal audits and management reviews.
desc.Cl.10: Improvement — Clause 10 requires the organisation to continually improve the suitability, adequacy, and effectiveness of its BCMS, including through the management of nonconformities and corrective actions.

about.title: ISO 22301:2019 — Business Continuity Management Systems
about.blurb: ISO 22301 specifies the requirements for planning, establishing, implementing, operating, monitoring, reviewing, maintaining, and continually improving a Business Continuity Management System (BCMS). It enables organisations to prepare for, respond to, and recover from disruptive incidents.

p: ISO 22301 follows the Annex SL high-level structure, making it compatible with ISO 27001 and ISO 9001. Clauses 4–10 contain the normative requirements for a BCMS.
The standard applies to organisations of all types and sizes that need to manage the continuity of their critical activities. Certification is available through accredited certification bodies.
